title: AMD Enters the Trillion-Dollar Quantum Computing Race, Partnering with PsiQuantum to Develop Infrastructure for Fault-Tolerant, Utility-Scale Systems!
excerpt: AMD has announced an expanded partnership with PsiQuantum to jointly design infrastructure capable of supporting fault-tolerant, utility-scale quantum computers!
content:
AMD has announced an expanded partnership with PsiQuantum to jointly design infrastructure capable of supporting fault-tolerant, utility-scale quantum computers. The deal comes as quantum computing attracts growing investor interest, with businesses and governments seeking systems that can solve scientific and commercial problems that are difficult for conventional computers to tackle. Technological breakthroughs have fuelled optimism about quantum computing’s potential applications in drug discovery, financial modelling and cryptography.

In May, the US Department of Commerce announced plans to invest a total of US$2 billion in minority stakes in nine quantum computing companies under the CHIPS Act, including a US$100 million deal with PsiQuantum. The expanded partnership builds on the companies’ existing research and development using AMD’s Versal FPGA family. It will integrate AMD Instinct GPUs, EPYC CPUs and the ROCm software stack with PsiQuantum’s silicon photonics quantum platform. As part of the deal, AMD also plans to make an equity investment of an undisclosed amount in PsiQuantum.

PsiQuantum’s CEO said quantum computing will work alongside artificial intelligence and high-performance computing to tackle problems in healthcare, materials, energy and finance that remain difficult to solve today. By bringing together their teams and technologies, PsiQuantum and AMD aim to advance the computing industry, developing the underlying infrastructure for utility-scale quantum systems while exploring new approaches to silicon photonics networking to support the scaling of next-generation AI.

The collaboration aligns with the US Department of Energy’s Quantum Genesis Priority Applications (QGPAs), which identify key scientific areas where fault-tolerant quantum computing could deliver practical benefits, including chemistry, materials, subatomic physics and applied mathematics.

PsiQuantum is currently an anchor tenant at the Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park in Chicago. AMD’s Chief Technology Officer said the partnership brings AMD’s full-stack computing and software capabilities to this emerging field, drawing on both companies’ strengths to accelerate the development of utility-scale quantum computing.

Market Insight:

Quantum computing still accounts for a relatively small share of technology giants’ research and development budgets. IBM has pledged to invest US$10 billion over the next five years, potentially making it the largest corporate investor in the field. IBM expects quantum investments to begin delivering measurable industrial value around 2028–2029.
